reason: The verse boasts of working the forge (கருமா னுலையிலே தீயை மூட்டுவோம்) and making gold (பொன்னை யாக்குவோம்), an alchemical transmutation claim; the finding that gold comes from mercury only by nuclear reactions, never by chemical or furnace processing, is evidence against it, though the lines may be partly figurative.
The verse wishes to stop letting the mind run to many places (பல இடத்தே மனதைப் பாயவிட்டு); mind-wandering is the shared topic, but the verse claims nothing about happiness.

The body is called coloured skin over a swarming nest of worms (புழுக் கூட்டின்மேல் வண்ணத் தோல்), a disgust image for renunciation; matching it to the body's bacterial population needs a generous literal reading.
The verse names the sushumna between ida and pingala (இடைபிங் கலைநடுவே) but claims no left-right alternation of airflow; reading the channels as nostrils is a gloss.
The verse claims meditation on the five letters makes the unstable body stable (தூலசடம் நிலைக்கும்); quantum nonlocality has no bearing on that.
The verse tells how to catch the running thought (ஓடித் திரியும் கருத்து) and still it in nada's space; meditation is the shared topic, but it claims no effect on anxiety, pain or mood.
The verse mocks those who melt metals and join lead with gold (வங்கமுக்தங்கஞ் சேர்த்து) as a disgrace; it shares the metals topic with the contamination finding but makes no claim about medicines.
A preface promising to teach drugs, salts and melted substances (சரக்கு, உருக்கினங்கள்); nothing about new neurons in adults.
The verse scorns the monkey mind (மனக்குரங்கு) of millions who call themselves yogis without knowing; meditation is the shared topic, but there is no claim about clinical outcomes.

The verse speaks of raising the fire (அங்கியை எழுப்பியே) through the channel past six lotuses; this is a kundalini cipher, and tying it to measured body heat in tummo needs a gloss the Tamil does not fix.

The verse says that through grace everything appeared false and the Lord alone true (யாவையுமெனக்குப் பொய்யெனத்தோன்றி); a revised view of the world shares a topic with the speculative relaxed-priors model, but nothing more.
The mirage that a deer takes for water (கானலைமான் நீரெனவே) is a simile for worldly delusion; perceptual error is the shared topic, but the verse makes no claim about how perception works.
The poet complains that hunger wrings his belly (பசிக்குதையா, பாழ்வயிறு); hunger is the shared topic, but the verse claims nothing about fasting's cellular effects.
The verse longs for the place where inquiry dries up (விசாரமது வற்றவிடம்); quiet thought is the shared topic with default-mode findings, but no specific claim is made.
Forgetting oneself in oneself (தன்னையும் தானே மறந்து) has nothing to do with the reliability of pulse diagnosis.
Breath (வாயு) at the gate where sun and moon move (தவனசோமர்) is cipher for the two breaths; the verse makes no claim about hemispheric or autonomic effects of one-nostril breathing.
Seeking the fourth state (நாலாம் பதம்) is a spiritual goal; brain waste clearance during sleep is unrelated.
Opening the fire-chamber (நெருப்பறை) to become the Lord is a yogic cipher; it makes no claim about body temperature or immunity.
An alchemical red calx (செந்தூரம்) that makes metals yield; nothing about sleep.
The Lord is said to be everywhere (எங்குமுள்ளோ) and the whole world his form; per the brief, pervasion of the One is not something Bell tests speak to.

The verse longs for the light of the eye and the light of the sky (விண்ணின் ஒளி) to be revealed; perceived lights are the shared topic with the adverse-experience survey, but the verse claims no outcome of practice.
A long satire stripping flattering comparisons from body parts (முலையைப் பார்த்து முளரிமொட்டு); it says nothing about where emotions are felt in the body.

The verse says that in the place of staying still (சும்மா இருந்தவிடம்) the poet does not see even himself (என்னையுங் காணேனே); a quieted self shares a topic with default-mode findings, but the verse is not a claim the finding tests.
The verse sets the mind in the suzhumunai as sun and moon exchange (பரிதிமதி); meditation is the shared topic, but the verse is not about repeating a word and its effects on the cortex.
The verse ties steady pranayama (பிராணாயம்) and mounting the vaasi to drinking nectar (அமிர்தபானம்); deathlessness is only implied, so the lifespan finding meets it only by topic.

The verse prescribes drawing the breath up the left channel and holding it (இடைகலையி லேற வாங்கிச் சுழுமுனையில் கும்பித்து), claiming this brings trance (சொக்கு வீரே); the finding bears on whether one-sided breathing has specific effects, but the evidence is inconsistent and reading இடைகலை as the left nostril is a gloss.
The two lights rising and setting at the root (இருசுடரும் உதித்தொடுங்கு) are a cipher for the breaths; the verse does not describe nostril alternation.
Handling cobras and making them spit poison (கடுவிஷங் கக்க) has nothing to do with quantum decoherence.
The verse claims chanting Sivayavasi (செபிக்க) brings every attainment and rule of the sky; mantra recitation is the shared topic, but the finding measures breathing rate, not powers.
Seeing as light in a mirror (கண்ணாடிக்குள் ஒளிபோல) is a simile for direct knowing, not a reported experience of light.
The verse calls pilgrimage egoism (ஆணவம்) and urges holding the Lord's feet within; nothing about predicting the body's internal state.
The light beyond the three times (காலமூன் றுங்கடந்த) is a mystical image; daily body clocks are unrelated.
Seeing the thousand and eight circles (ஆயிரத்தெட்டு வட்டம்) is a yogic vision; nothing about heartbeat detection.
The body is called an unstable pot filled with wind (நிலையற்ற பாண்டம்); impermanence of the body is the shared topic with cell turnover, but the verse is a moral lament, not a claim about renewal.
The verse urges holding in mind the triple void beyond the three faculties (முப்பொறிக்கு எட்டாத முப்பாழ்); meditative emptiness shares a topic with the speculative model only.

The verse dismisses furnace-processed arsenic (பாஷாணம்) with 'what is there in it' (இருப்பதென்னடி), denying the value of the preparation; the finding of heavy-metal poisonings linked to Siddha and Ayurvedic preparations bears on that scepticism and supports it.

The verse places the five letters within the breath-horse (வாசி பரிக்குள் நின்றது மஞ்செழுத்தாம்), linking mantra and breath; the finding links recitation to slow breathing, but the verse states a mystical identity, not an effect.

The verse asks whether caste is marked on flesh, skin or bone (இறைச்சிதோல் எலும்பினும் இலக்கமிட்டு இருக்குதோ), denying a bodily basis for caste; the finding of shared mixed ancestry and late onset of endogamy bears on this and largely supports it, though endogamy since then has left group-level genetic differences.
The poet's hunger grips his belly (பசிக்குதையா); hunger is the shared topic, but the verse makes no claim about fasting schedules.
The light within the ruby (மாணிக்கத்துள்ளொளி) is a devotional image, not a report of meditative visual phenomena.
